criteria.note: The non-LLM mirror RUNNER (.warp/tracker_mirror_runner.py) DRIVES the shipped one-way mirror and adds NO projection rule of its own. reconcile(events, config, spec_index, plan_index, adapter) is the pure core: it materializes the stream once (events = list(events), a generator is single-pass) and feeds BOTH mirror_events (spec lifecycle: status, comments, artifact links, the ready-to-test reassign) and mirror_plan_events (plan structure: epic + children) from tracker_mirror.py (WARP-0605/0606 + the WARP-1004 reassign/links). run_from_repo is the thin production wrapper: it reads the stream through an INJECTED reader (default _default_event_reader over the durable .warp/events.jsonl, a fixture list in the gate), loads the tracker config via load_tracker_config, and builds the spec/plan indices via build_spec_index/build_plan_index over the REPOSITORY (the source of truth). It is a RECONCILER (recompute the desired tracker state each pass and apply it) with NO processed-offset ledger and NO second store, and it writes ONLY through the injected adapter; no path in the runner writes a spec or plan file (indices are read-only, load_tracker_config is read-only). Selftest drives run_from_repo with an injected reader asserted called exactly once with the fixture path (parsed one way) and injected spec+plan indices, and both mirrors fire from ONE stream (child:PLAN-0010:W5 reaches Done AND epic:PLAN-0010 is created with warp_repo repo-a).

OPT-IN and OFF BY DEFAULT, no rogue process, verified structurally not just by promise. The runner is invoked explicitly as `warp mirror` (bin/warp gains it in KNOWN_SUBCOMMANDS and a route that calls tracker_mirror_runner._cli after a repo-only presence check, byte-identical across plugin/templates and all six packs, single md5 7164e7f0 over eight copies). Actual imports are argparse, importlib.util, json, sys, pathlib only: no subprocess, no os.fork, no os.system, no os.exec, no Popen, no threading, no daemon, no atexit/signal, no scheduler, no systemd/crontab, no network of its own (the docstring mentions urllib only to say the ADAPTER owns REST). Each `warp mirror` invocation is ONE reconcile pass (poll-when-run); a cadence is the operator's own re-run, never a hidden mechanism. Installing WARP lays no timer/daemon/auto-start. Same off-by-default posture as the fleet supervisor (WARP-0907). Selftest asserts warp mirror --dry-run routes to the runner (rc 0, one pass, no network), the runner is repo-only (not in the shipped engine set yet present in the repo, so a pack that did not lay it fails loud rather than importing a missing module), and the source imports no process-spawning module.

The live JiraCloud adapter is completed HONESTLY as a reference path and fails closed. JiraCloudAdapter._assign (.warp/tracker_intake.py) now PUTs /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/assignee with {"accountId": assignee} (the WARP-1004 deferral gone, the raise removed), beside the already-live _comment (POST) and _set_status (POST transition). The token is resolved from token_ref AT CONSTRUCTION (__init__ line 311) and the adapter FAILS CLOSED there (TrackerAdapterError 'no token resolved from ...') before any write, so the assign is never reached without a credential and no raw credential appears in a file/prompt/proof/log. build_live_adapter(config) constructs this reference adapter from the connection block (base_url + token_ref, optional email) and surfaces the fail-closed by name (MirrorRunnerError). This live path needs a real Jira, so it is NOT run in the gate (the FakeTracker path is what the gate runs), matching the other reference adapters. Epic/child creation stays deferred: _create_or_update_epic and _create_or_update_child still RAISE, now naming WARP-1006. Selftest teeth: build_live_adapter raises when the token_ref resolves no secret and CONSTRUCTS a JiraCloudAdapter (with an assign method) when the env secret resolves, no network at construction; the source is asserted to have dropped the WARP-1005 assign deferral (PUT assignee remains) and to still carry the WARP-1006 epic/child deferral.

Idempotency is proven offline over the FakeTracker with REAL, load-bearing teeth. A GROWING stream advances the ticket: pass 1 (ready only) -> mapped ready 'To Do', reassignments 0; pass 2 (ready+verdict) -> 'In Review', reassigned to the reviewer (reporter default) once, artifact links posted once; pass 3 (ready+verdict+shipped) -> 'Done', transitions 1. A full REPLAY plus a DOUBLED event (ready,verdict,ship,ship) records NO new transition/comment/reassign (all 0) and leaves state_digest byte-identical. NON-TAUTOLOGY: on a FRESH tracker the ready-only stream stays at ready with NO assignee, and only the grown stream advances and reassigns, so the advance is caused by the stream, not by the runner always writing. TEETH PROVEN BY MUTATION: disabling FakeTracker._set_status's no-op-when-unchanged guard turned the two runner replay cases RED ('records no new transition/comment/reassign' and 'leaves state byte-identical') at 1436 passed / 14 failed; git checkout of .warp/tracker_adapter.py reverted it, git diff --quiet clean, HEAD still e6859e7, selftest back at 1450 / 0. There is no offset ledger and no second store; the events are the truth and the tracker converges to them.

The index CONTENT (the WARP-1005 shipped row, the frontier, the plan rollup) is byte-identical. I restored specs/index.md, .warp/last_verify, and .warp/events.jsonl to their commit state; the tree carries only proof/WARP-1005/.

Non-blocking, inherited behavior the runner now applies live. The ready-to-test handoff (reassign + artifact links) that the runner drives is gated on the PRESENCE of verdict.recorded anywhere in the deduped stream, not on in_review being the child's latest mapped status (carried from WARP-1004). A single fresh reconcile pass over an already-terminal stream (verdict.recorded then spec.shipped) therefore performs both the terminal transition and the handoff in one pass. This is correct and idempotent (by-target reassign, keyed comment; matches the AC4 replay teeth), so it is correctness-preserving; worth noting only so an operator running the live mirror knows the handoff is presence-triggered.
